newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Commission agrees six-nation EU invitation list.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission agrees six-nation EU invitation list.

text.p: The European Commission agreed on Tuesday that Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia should join Cyprus in entry talks for the European Union's first expansion into eastern Europe.
"It has been adopted," Commission Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas told Reuters referring to the Commission's Agenda 2000 document, adopted without much discussion at a meeting of the EU executive.
The document will be formally presented to the European Parliament on Wednesday.

The decision came as no suprise after the 20 Commissioners last week settled deep differences over how many east European countries to recommend should join Cyprus in the EU's most ambitious expansion since its foundation.

The Agenda 2000 document sets out the expansion plan and the policy changes the EU will have to make to accommodate radically different countries and says that five other applicants -- Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Romania -- should be left to prepare for membership at their own pace.
They will each have so-called contractual accession partnerships.
Cyprus had already been promised membership talks next year.
The document, obtained by Reuters ahead of the decision, tells the East European applicants they have to make more economic efforts before they cross the threshold.

The changes precribed in the paper for the existing 15-nation EU involve a new inter-governmental conference soon after 2000 to overhaul the EU's decision-making procedures to prevent paralysis in a bloc with 21 members.

The EU's June 16-17 Amsterdam summit failed to agree on how to revise the way decisions are taken ahead of enlargement, but said a new overhaul would be necessary if the bloc extended to more than 20 members.
A radical reform of the EU's Common Agriculture Policy is also prescribed in the document, with drastic cuts of 10 percent in EU guaranteed prices for milk and 20 percent for cereals.
The EU executive says the EU should live under the current ceiling of the member states' financing until 2006.
The Commission's proposal will not be the last word on who will negotiate EU entry as it could be overturned by EU governments, which have different national interests at stake.
A final decision will be taken by EU leaders at their Luxembourg summit in December.
